project.name: Intentive
project.description: Intentive is a macOS-first desktop AI product. Its native SwiftUI app captures and organizes local context, persists memory on the Mac, and communicates with a local agent runtime bundled under desktop/macos/agent; a bounded FastAPI backend supplies supporting network and compute services.

nodes.name: agent-runtime-contract.schema.json
nodes.summary: Defines the strict JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 contract for Omi Agent Runtime v1. It requires context snapshots, tool-result envelopes and invocations, permission decisions, lifecycle states, failure taxonomy, an 8 KiB session-listing budget, and conformance scenarios for desktop-chat and realtime-voice adapters.
nodes.languageNotes: JSON Schema uses const and enum constraints, minimum cardinalities, and additionalProperties=false to enforce a closed runtime contract.

tour.title: macOS Entry and State
tour.description: OmiApp.swift is where the macOS process enters the product: it defines application lifecycle, authentication state, menu-bar commands, and startup maintenance. AppState.swift is the shared state owner that the rest of the desktop UI and services read and update. Together they establish who starts the app and where app-wide state lives.

tour.title: Native Window and UI Shell
tour.description: Once the process has an owner, DesktopHomeView.swift presents the main SwiftUI surface and coordinates navigation, state presentation, and interactions. DesktopNavigation.swift describes page destinations and navigation requests, while DesktopWindowLayoutPolicy.swift keeps window geometry and layout decisions in one place. This is the visual shell that turns app state into a usable Mac window.

tour.title: Capture and Live Transcription
tour.description: AudioCaptureService.swift owns the desktop audio capture boundary. LiveTranscriptMonitor.swift watches the live transcript surface, and LocalTranscriptionService.swift handles the local transcription-facing workflow. Read these after the shell to see how microphone or system audio becomes text that the app can display, while keeping capture and transcription in the macOS voice layer.

tour.title: Push-to-Talk and Realtime Voice
tour.description: PushToTalkManager.swift handles explicit push-to-talk input, while RealtimeHubController+PushToTalk.swift connects that gesture to the realtime hub. RealtimeHubController.swift coordinates provider lifecycle, turn routing, tool calls, audio state, and floating-control-bar integration. This path is distinct from ambient listening: it is the direct voice conversation control surface.

tour.title: Desktop Automation and Proactive Behavior
tour.description: DesktopAutomationBridge.swift is the handoff for desktop actions. ProactiveAssistantsPlugin.swift and AssistantCoordinator.swift organize proactive assistant behavior and coordinate assistant work. After seeing voice input, this step shows how the Mac can turn context into automation or proactive behavior, still inside the macOS capture, voice, and automation layer.

tour.title: Conversation Finalization and Local Storage
tour.description: After a conversation or capture produces useful turns, ConversationFinalizationService.swift owns finalization in the Mac client. LocalChatCatalog.swift keeps the local chat catalog that the UI can reopen and browse. This is the handoff from active interaction to durable Mac-local conversation state; it is not the hosted FastAPI backend.

tour.title: Rewind and Local Memory Retrieval
tour.description: RewindOnlyView.swift is the small entry surface for starting local Rewind monitoring and opening the full app. RewindDatabase.swift owns the SQLite lifecycle, migrations, recovery, persistence, search, and retention, while RewindIndexer.swift turns captures into searchable OCR, embedding, and metadata records. Together they explain how the Mac retrieves local memory later, rather than asking the backend to be the memory authority.

tour.title: Desktop Chat-to-Agent Bridge
tour.description: AgentBridge.swift and AgentClient.swift are the desktop chat-to-agent bridge. They give the Swift app a narrow client-side path to send chat work and receive agent results, while AgentRuntimeProcess.swift represents the process lifecycle that the desktop controls. This boundary connects the Swift UI to the local agent runtime without collapsing either side into the FastAPI backend.

tour.title: macOS Local Agent Runtime
tour.description: index.ts is the real entry point for the process under desktop/macos/agent: it wires tool relays, pending calls, ownership checks, JSONL transport, and the runtime kernel. kernel.ts exposes the runtime kernel API, and kernel-core.ts owns run, attempt, binding, transaction, and recovery state. This macOS Local Agent Runtime is bundled with the Mac app and is not a separate cross-platform product.

tour.title: FastAPI Backend Boundary
tour.description: Once the local desktop side needs hosted capabilities, backend/main.py creates the FastAPI application, registers routers and middleware, and manages startup and shutdown work. backend/routers/desktop_chat.py is the HTTP boundary for desktop chat requests and responses. This hosted backend is a supporting service boundary; it is separate from the Mac-local agent process in Step 9.

tour.title: Live STT Compute
tour.description: Live STT continues through backend/utils/stt/streaming.py, which handles streaming transport, admission, provider events, usage accounting, and cleanup. backend/utils/stt/vad_gate.py applies voice-activity gating so speech frames are admitted according to explicit state and policy. These files complete the story from Mac audio and voice controls to hosted transcription compute, without treating the backend as the local agent.
